_what: Daily XLMUSDT closes, the input to check-params.ts's realized-volatility measurement.
It is a file rather than a constant in the script because D-53's finding was that a hard-coded
sigma band was wrong by a factor of two at the low end, and every parameter derived from it was
wrong with it - the five planned vaults priced at 7.3 bps against a 28 bps floor, none of them
fillable by a rational counterparty. A committed series is also auditable: a reviewer can see
CORRECTED 2026-08-20. The first version of this file ended on a PROVISIONAL candle: it was
fetched at 21:58 UTC on 19 August, and the exchange's newest daily row is always the one still
in progress. That row read 0.17170 and 19 August actually closed at 0.17030, so the last day's
move was recorded as +10.85 % when it was +9.94 %, and 30-day sigma as 51.11 % when it was
49.01 %. Every row is now filtered on its own close time having passed, and the fetch asks for
one extra row so dropping the live one still leaves a full window.
The arithmetic was never wrong and three of us checked it; what none of us asked was whether
the last row was final. A number can be reproducible, independently verified and still measure
something that had not finished happening.
This is a point-in-time measurement, like deployments/environment-testnet.json. Re-fetch before
a real deploy; check-params.ts reads whatever series it is given and does not know how old this
source: Binance spot klines, GET /api/v3/klines?symbol=XLMUSDT&interval=1d&limit=92, rows with an unelapsed close time discarded
